_comment: A chain: a senior backend live-coding round, as real LeetCode design problems. Each keeps some state, changes it on a call, and has a rule that must stay true. Solve them in order, in a single sitting, talking as in the interview: restate the problem, state the rule, write the simplest solution that works, say where it breaks, fix it, test it, then say what changes at ten times the load. state = what is kept, event = what happens on a call, invariant = what must stay true. Rebuilt 2026-10-08 from the cached editorials in research/doocs-leetcode (the 2026-10-07 draft of invented drills was withdrawn: the questions were made up and the seq rule in Order Status From Events was incoherent). The ordering follows the clist rating.

2043.title: Simple Bank System
2043.event: check the account numbers and the balance, then move the money
2043.invariant: a balance never goes below zero; an invalid account changes nothing

1656.title: Design an Ordered Stream
1656.state: a slot per id and a pointer to the first empty slot
1656.event: insert fills its slot, then releases from the pointer while the slot is filled
1656.invariant: every id below the pointer has been released, in id order
1656.change: the check is a gap in the ids, not a balance; out-of-order arrivals wait in their slot until the gap fills

1396.title: Design Underground System
1396.state: per rider: the open check-in; per route: total time and trip count
1396.event: check-out closes the rider's record and adds its time to the route
1396.invariant: the average is total divided by count, never recomputed from trips
1396.change: two tables: per-key open state, and an aggregate kept as a running sum

1797.title: Design Authentication Manager
1797.event: generate sets now + ttl; renew does the same only while unexpired; count scans the expiries
1797.invariant: a token is live exactly when its expiry is after now
1797.change: the record is a time, and the check compares it with now

981.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
981.state: per key: the list of (time, value) in set order
981.event: set appends; get binary-searches for the last time at or before the query
981.invariant: each key's list is sorted by time because set times strictly increase
981.change: keep every version with its time instead of the latest; read by binary search

146.title: LRU Cache
146.state: a dict from key to node, and a doubly linked list in recency order
146.event: get moves the node to the front; put inserts at the front and evicts the tail over capacity
146.invariant: the list order is the recency order, and the dict and the list hold the same keys
146.change: eviction, by use instead of by time; the order lives in a linked list so a move is O(1)

1801.title: Number of Orders in the Backlog
1801.state: a max-heap of buy orders and a min-heap of sell orders
1801.event: a new order takes from the other side's top while the prices cross; what is left rests on its own heap
1801.invariant: the heaps hold only unmatched orders and each top is that side's best price
1801.change: two heaps instead of a list; matching is a loop on the other side's top

2034.title: Stock Price Fluctuation
2034.state: price per timestamp, the latest timestamp, and a max-heap and min-heap of (price, timestamp)
2034.event: update overwrites the price for its timestamp; maximum and minimum pop the top while it disagrees with the table
2034.invariant: a heap top is answered only when the table still holds that price at that timestamp
2034.change: updates arrive out of order and correct earlier ones; the table is the truth and stale heap entries are skipped when they surface

3508.title: Implement Router
3508.state: a set of packets in the router, a FIFO deque with a capacity, and per destination a timestamp list plus a count of forwarded packets
3508.event: add refuses a duplicate and evicts the oldest at capacity; forward pops the front; getCount binary-searches the timestamps
3508.invariant: the set holds exactly the packets in the deque
3508.change: dedupe by a key in a set, and a capacity that evicts the oldest; the count query is a binary search over times

1348.title: Tweet Counts Per Frequency
1348.state: per name: the sorted times of its records
1348.event: record inserts a time; the query counts each bucket by two binary searches
1348.change: a count per window bucket instead of a single lookup; the window is sliced by binary search
